Frequently Asked Questions

Half the houses on my Greer street have replaced their AC. Should I think about replacing mine?

Same-vintage neighborhoods do fail in clusters, so nearby replacements are useful information rather than a verdict. An inspection establishes your unit’s actual condition, and if replacement is close, planning it beats meeting it in July. Preemptive replacement of a healthy system, though, rarely pencils out.

Is a dual fuel system worth it over a standard heat pump in Greer?

It depends on gas availability and how you weight the coldest weeks, so the comparison gets run with your utility rates. The heat pump carries most of the winter economically either way; dual fuel adds gas heat for the stretch when heat pump output costs the most. The quote shows both configurations.

My sump pump only matters a few days a year. How do I know it will work?

Test it, and have it serviced annually. A pump that sits idle for months can seize or stick exactly when the rain arrives, and the failure announces itself as a flooded crawl space. Battery backup earns consideration here because the storms that flood are the storms that cut power.

What does an electrician check before installing an EV charger?

Panel capacity, available breaker space, and the run from panel to garage. The charger’s circuit is a continuous high draw, so the evaluation confirms the panel can carry it alongside existing load. If it cannot, the upgrade gets quoted before the charger, not after it trips.

Which communities around Greer do you serve?

Regular routes cover Taylors, Duncan, and Five Forks, plus the rest of the Greenville and Spartanburg footprint. The chat team can verify any address.
